name: Pet Parents Dubai
about: Vets, groomers, pet-friendly cafes and heat tips for dogs and cats across Dubai. Puppy photos welcome, judgement not.

stories.author: p05
stories.text: Puppy finally slept through the night. Miracles happen 🐶

stories.author: p10
stories.text: Dog beach hour in JBR is back. Bring water and a towel for paws.

stories.author: p07
stories.text: Found a cat sitter in Mirdif who sends daily photos. Five stars.

posts.author: p05
posts.text: Vet nurse here. Quick reminder for everyone: summer means tick and flea checks every two weeks, even for indoor pets. The heat makes them more active than you think.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks Mariam, I thought indoor dogs were safe. Booking a check this week.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Cats too? Mine is strictly indoor and somehow still attracts fleas. Mystery.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: The flea spray at the vet worked for us. Ask for the one that's safe for puppies.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Do you know a clinic that does checks on weekends? Work hours are killing me.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Ticks in Dubai in summer? Didn't know. Adding a check to the weekly routine.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Check behind the ears and between the toes after every walk. Takes 30 seconds.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: My cat hates the flea comb more than the vet visit. Dramatic little creature.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Cats are drama queens, but yes, check them. Flea treatment is cheaper than a bad week.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @mariam_s which spray is the puppy-safe one? I'd love the exact name for the clinic.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: @sarak I'll post a list with the clinic names in a separate thread, to be safe.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thank you, a list is much better than guessing. Please include the prices too.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: My dog had fleas last summer after one park visit. Lesson learned, I check now.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Parks are the main source, no question. Shoes off at the door helps too.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Heat check: dogs are not allowed on hot tiles, the vet clinic says the same.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Adding a note: the cat carrier should live out, not in the cupboard. Cats get used to it.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Great reminder. Summer heat and parasites are a double hit, be vigilant.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: My baker's heart melts at every pet photo. Keep these tips coming, Mariam.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee shop cat has a flea collar on, the owner says it works. Just a thought.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Puppy is on the flea plan since last week, he is not a fan but it's fine.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Every pet is different, so ask your vet before using any product. Sorry for the rules.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Good call, always check the label for the animal's weight. Keep it safe.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Keeping the checklist in my phone now. Thanks for making it easy to follow.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Puppy has the best vet nurse in the city. Lucky pup.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks all, saving this post. Pets are family, let's keep them healthy.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Health first, fun second. Yalla, check those paws today 🐾

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Looking for a pet-friendly cafe in Mirdif or Al Warqa where I can bring my cat in a carrier. Patio preferred, but a quiet corner with AC is fine too.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Cats in carriers on the patio are common at one cafe near the park. Ask for the corner table.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Cats on the patio? Brave. My vet clinic would approve of a quiet corner, though.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Our coffee shop in Al Quoz is cat-friendly, not with food, just the calm.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dogs are allowed on most patios, cats need a carrier. Check the cafe rules first.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: My cat would hate any cafe, so I'll be the one with the photos from the doorway.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Mirdif has a few options near the park. The one with the big windows is lovely.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cat cafes are a niche here, but a pet-friendly patio is becoming more common.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: I'd bring a travel blanket for the carrier, cats love the smell of home.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for the tip on the travel blanket, Sara. Very practical advice.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @sarak thanks! Do you know the name of the one with the windows?

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I think it's the one by the old souk side. Check the map, it has great coffee too.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Share the name when you find it, I'll add it to the vet clinic list for owners.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee and cats in one place is my dream. I'd happily roast beans for a cat cafe.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A cat cafe would do very well in Dubai, the summer is long and cats love the AC.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Cats prefer the AC, that's the one thing I know for sure. Good luck Anjali.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Patio plus carrier plus coffee sounds like a fun Saturday. Count me in for the pet meetup.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Pet meetups are great for socialising the dogs. Maybe a monthly one in the park.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A monthly meetup is a great idea. Sign me up with the puppy and the cafe crowd.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: I'll start a poll in the group for a cat-friendly meetup date, thanks everyone.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Bring treats for the cat and a little cake for the humans, pastry chef's rule.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will be a very polite guest. He is training with treats right now.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the meetup pet-friendly and quiet. Everyone's animals will thank you.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Quiet corner, good coffee, happy cat. Simple and beautiful.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Looking forward to meeting the pets. The puppy and I are in for a long walk after.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's finish with a group photo of all the pets. The cat will be the star.

posts.author: p06
posts.text: My cat knocked a glass off the table three times this week. Is this normal behaviour or should I be worried? She looks very pleased with herself about it.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Cats do this to check if you're watching. It's normal, but keep the glass away from the edge.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: My cat does it to the mug every morning. We have a ritual now, lol.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: It's play and attention seeking. Give her a toy at the same time to redirect it.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pretty sure mine is trying to test gravity for science. Very thorough researcher.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: If it happens a lot, check for boredom. Try a short play session before bed.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Mine knocks things off the counter when she is hungry. Check the feeding schedule.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: My cat does it right after I sit down with coffee. Clearly she is a professional.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'd speak to the vet if it's sudden, though. Changes in behaviour can mean a health thing.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Agree with Hannah, sudden changes are worth a check. Usually it's just play though.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: @mariam_s it's been going on for only a week, she eats well and sleeps well. I'll keep an eye on it.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: A week is fine to observe. If she starts drinking more or losing weight, call the vet.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Cats are masters of mischief. A cat with a plan is a happy cat.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Hide the glasses, buy a cat tower, and enjoy the show. That's my advice.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Cat tower is a game changer. Mine uses it as a lookout post now.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Puppy would never knock a glass, he would drink from it. Different species.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee mug survival is a daily challenge in this flat. I feel your pain.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Maybe she wants water. Try a fountain, many cats prefer running water.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Water fountain was a hit for my cat. She drinks more and stops knocking things over.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Running water helps, and a toy near the glass area keeps her busy.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep a routine of play in the evening, and she'll calm down during the day.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thanks all, the cat tower and the water fountain are on my shopping list today.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Mariam, thanks for the reassurance. Cat is now sleeping in the sun, looking innocent.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: That innocent look is the most dangerous one. Enjoy the peace while it lasts.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck Kwame, cats are very clever. Let us know how the fountain goes.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: The cat has won this round, but I'm keeping my mug on the far side of the table.

posts.author: p01
posts.text: Weekend dog grooming in Al Barsha: I took my golden retriever for a bath and the groomer used a gentle shampoo. He came back smelling like a fresh croissant. Recommend?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Smelling like a croissant is the ultimate praise. Name of the groomer please?

comments.author: p05
comments.text: A gentle shampoo is key, too much soap dries the skin. Good find, Sara.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Smell like a croissant? I'll take him as my new pastry assistant, lol.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dogs with long coats need regular brushing between baths. Ask for a de-shedding session.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee after the grooming session is the best, the dog and the human both deserve it.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our groomer does a lovely job but the wait is long on Saturdays. Book a week ahead.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dogs hate the dryer, so ask for a towel dry and gentle blow dry. Less stress for the pup.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: My husky sheds like a snowstorm. The de-shed treatment changed my living room.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Ask the groomer about ear cleaning too, golden retrievers get ear infections easily.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @anjali_rao yes, they cleaned his ears too, and trimmed the nails. Full service.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Nails are the one thing I always forget. Glad you mentioned it, Sara.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: The groomer should also check for ticks while they wash, double win.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ticks and croissants in one visit, this is a complete service, I love it.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's first grooming is next week. Please wish him luck, he is very dramatic.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dramatic dogs are my favourite kind. Good luck, Mariam.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A calm dog makes for a calm groomer. Treats during the session help a lot.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Could you share the price range? Trying to budget for a monthly visit.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @hannah_b about 150 AED for a full wash with trim in Al Barsha. Prices change, check first.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Good to know. I'll ask for a quote before I book, so there are no surprises.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Quote first is always wise. A good groomer will tell you the full price upfront.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: My dog gets the deluxe package once a month, it's worth every dirham.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dogs who get regular grooming are calmer, I've seen it in the pool too.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ok, the croissant dog is the reason I'm adopting one. Sara, you've won this thread.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the croissant smell, he's been sniffing my bag all day.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Enjoy the fresh smell and the happy dog. Good weekend, everyone.

posts.author: p09
posts.text: Pet insurance in the UAE: has anyone compared the plans? I'm trying to decide between basic cover for accidents only and a plan that includes routine checks.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Accident-only is cheaper but routine checks add up fast. Compare the annual limits first.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Read the exclusions carefully, pre-existing conditions are usually not covered.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: I went with a mid-tier plan. Two vet visits in one year already paid for it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Ask the vet clinic which providers they work with, they often know the claims process well.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim coaches see a lot of injuries in dogs at the beach, so I'd go for the broader cover.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pet insurance sounds very grown up. My cat's insurance is her biggest expense, honestly.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Check the waiting period too. Some plans take weeks before they start paying out.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Monthly premium versus annual, the annual one is cheaper in my experience.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd rather spend on coffee for the owner than insurance, but I'm a bad example.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: @omar_q that's a good point about the beach injuries. Thanks for the heads up.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy needs the broader cover, he eats everything from the sand. Very expensive hobby.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dog-specific plans may be better than a general pet plan. Compare both.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Keep the receipts and photos of every visit. Claims go faster with clean paperwork.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Check if the plan covers emergency vet visits at night, that's the one that matters most.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Emergency cover saved us once at midnight. Worth more than the premium, honestly.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good luck with the decision, Hannah. Whichever you choose, the pet is lucky to have you.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thank you all, this is a much better summary than the brochures.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Insurance for coffee beans would be my dream plan, but let's stick with pets.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: I'll post a comparison table for the group once I have the quotes. Stay tuned.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Looking forward to it. Maybe add a column for the waiting period too.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Insurance is the boring part, but it's the one that saves you when it matters.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Well said, Ravi. Boring but essential. Like the vaccines.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Vaccines first, insurance second, treats third. The order matters.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks everyone, I'm going to compare three plans this weekend and share the result.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Good luck Hannah, and remember, the dog is always the best investment in the end.

posts.author: p08
posts.text: Our coffee shop is starting a dog-friendly corner on the terrace this weekend. Water bowls, shade, and a sign saying please pick up after your dog. Feedback welcome!

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Yes! A water bowl is the most important thing on a terrace in summer. Well done, Yusuf.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will be the first customer, he already knows the coffee smell. Thank you!

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dog-friendly with cake on the menu would be perfect. Maybe a dog biscuit too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Shade is crucial. Put a fan near the corner, dogs get hot even on a mild day.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for doing this. Running with my dog and then coffee, the dream routine.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good clear sign, the dog owners who ignore the rules are the real problem.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Please keep the dogs off the chairs. Cats too, if any cat wants to visit, lol.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Maybe add a small bowl of water for cats as well, they are welcome on the terrace.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'll bring the team for a dog-friendly meeting, the terrace will be packed.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @hannah_b a team meeting with dogs sounds like a good concept for a startup, honest.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the terrace calm in the afternoon too, the dogs need a rest in the heat.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is practising his sit for the terrace. Two treats per sit, he is very motivated.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Puppy with a flour dusted nose is the new coffee shop mascot. I'm volunteering.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thanks Yusuf for the sign. Clear rules, good manners, happy dogs. That's the formula.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Ask your staff to be kind to nervous dogs too, some of them need space.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Dog music on the terrace? Kidding, but a calm playlist helps animals relax.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Let's organise a first meetup there next weekend, the timing is perfect.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I'll bring my dog for the first meetup, he loves coffee smells even if he can't drink it.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A dog's first coffee is always a surprise. Make sure it is only the water bowl.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Water only for the dogs, promise. Espresso is for the humans, that's the policy.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the policy. He is already practising his best calm face.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dog-friendly coffee shops are good for the neighbourhood. Good job, Yusuf.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Yes, the neighbourhood needs more places like this. Pets are part of the community.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for the great work, the group is proud to support the terrace.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: See you at the meetup, Yusuf. Bring the good beans and the water bowl 🐶

posts.author: p10
posts.text: Heat safety for pets, a quick checklist: walk before 8am or after 7pm, test pavement with your hand for seven seconds, carry water, and never leave a pet in a parked car.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Seven seconds on the pavement is the rule the clinic teaches too. Great summary, Omar.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Never in a parked car, even for two minutes. Please, everyone, this is serious.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Carrying water is so important. I keep a collapsible bowl in every bag now.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Early morning walks are my routine, it works for both of us and the streets are cool.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Shade and water, plus a cooling mat for the bed. My cat loves it more than the AC.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Signs of heatstroke in pets include heavy panting, drooling and weakness. Call the vet.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee shops should have a pet water station, it's a simple kindness. Adding it to my list.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Pets left on the balcony in the heat is a risk too. Bring them inside on hot days.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our office has a dog-friendly policy but the parking lot is hot. Guess the lift is the answer.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @hannah_b the lift is safe, but not the car park. Good instinct.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's cooling vest is the best purchase of this year. He looks like a little lifeguard.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Lifeguard puppy with a cooling vest. That's the next viral picture for sure.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Shade in the garden plus a fan and water. Simple and effective, my dog is calm.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for the checklist Omar, I'm pinning this for the next summer.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Heat stroke in pets can happen fast. Learn the signs and act quickly, always.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Keep the vet number in your phone and the nearest 24-hour clinic too.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee to go in the heat is a risk for the dog too, keep the cup away from paws.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good tip, Yusuf. Hot drinks and curious paws are a bad combination.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Adding a pet emergency number to my phone home screen now. Thank you, Omar.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good idea. Keep safety information visible, not buried in a chat.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy says thanks for the water tip. He drinks a lot after the walks.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dogs and water bowls are the best pair. Let's make this the rule everywhere.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: This should be pinned at the top of the group. Thanks for the clear list.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Stay cool everyone, and check on your neighbours' pets too in the heat.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Let's all be the kind neighbour who knocks if a pet looks in trouble. Yalla 🐾

comments.text: That is the best news I've read this week. Foster heroes, you did so well.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Congrats to the kitten and the family. Sunbeam nap is the true sign of happiness.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Tears of joy. Thank you Layla for giving him a safe start. The sunbeam photo is perfect.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Fostering is hard work, so good on you for doing it. Well done!

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Happy ending, lovely to hear. The kitten is lucky to have you.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Sunbeam cats are the happiest cats. Mine has claimed the same spot for years.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd add a coffee to the celebration, but I'm sure the cake is the real star today.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: What a wonderful post to read on a Monday. Thank you for sharing the update.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good job Layla. Fostering saves lives, and so does sharing the good news.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thank you all, it was a team effort with the vet clinic and the family. So grateful.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: The clinic cared for him from day one. Fostering is a family project, really.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Who is the new family? Can we see more photos of the kitten in the new home?

comments.author: p03

comments.text: Kids and kittens are the perfect combo. Hope he gets all the sunbeams.

comments.text: We have fostered three puppies so far. It is hard, but every goodbye is worth it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Please share how to start fostering, I want to try next year. Any tips?

comments.author: p05

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee and fostering, a good combo. Hope the kitten finds the best morning routine.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Adding fostering to my list of things to do next year. Hannah's office could sponsor a pet fund.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A pet fund at the office is a great idea, let's talk about it at the next lunch.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Running and fostering, the two things I didn't know I needed. Good luck to all of you.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Puppy and the kitten, a playdate? Mariam, please, I need a sequel.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would love a playdate, but the kitten should have a quiet week first. Patience!

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thank you all, my heart is full. Yalla, let's celebrate with a pet-friendly cake 🎂

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Layla, you're a legend. Congratulations to the whole rescue team 🐾

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Question for cat owners: how do you keep the litter smell under control in a small flat? We've tried three brands and the smell still sneaks through to the living room.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Scoop daily and change the box every two weeks. Silica litter is worth the price, honestly.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Put the tray in the bathroom with the fan on, that's my trick. Smell goes straight out.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Baking soda under the litter, a thin layer. It helped in my tiny kitchen flat.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A covered tray with a filter is better than an open one. Less smell, less spreading.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Check the cat's diet too, some foods change the smell. Ask your vet for advice.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Keep the tray away from the kitchen, the smell mixes with the food smell. Not nice.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd add an air purifier near the tray. Cheap and quiet, my flat smells like coffee now.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: We tried a robot litter box. Expensive, but the smell is much better now.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Cats are very sensitive to dirty trays. A clean tray often solves the problem completely.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Thanks all, the bathroom idea and the baking soda are my plan for this week.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @tomasz_n also check the flat's ventilation, a small window open helps a lot.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Mango would like a cleaner tray, she has opinions about everything, honestly.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pastry chef's rule: clean the tray as often as you clean the mixer. No excuses.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Cats notice everything, so the smell matters to them as much as to us.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: A pet deodoriser is safe if it's cat-friendly. Read the label and avoid strong sprays.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Ventilation and cleanliness, the basics that work. Thank you for the reminder.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee grounds are not litter, though I'm sure someone has tried it. Please don't.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Ha, a coffee litter experiment. Yusuf, you are very creative.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the litter box clean and the living room will smell like home, not like the box.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck with the trial, I'll report back which combo worked best.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Report back with the brand name too, the group will want to know.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy has never had a litter problem, he prefers the balcony. Different challenges.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Balcony is a great solution if you have one, the cat is very impressed with the view.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thanks Tomasz, the group has so many great ideas. I'll try the bathroom tray too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good luck, and enjoy the fresh flat. Yalla, happy cat, happy home 🐈

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Weekend dog park meetup at Mushrif this Saturday morning, 7am, shaded area near the play zone. Small dogs and big dogs welcome, but please keep them on leash until you say hi.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will be there, he is bouncing with excitement already. See you Saturday!

comments.author: p02
